label: Compliance costs of won rules, from the regulators' own impact analyses (ours)

rows.label: EPA oil and gas methane rule (2023): net compliance cost a year, 2024-2038 (2019 dollars)

source.title: US EPA (2023), Regulatory Impact Analysis for the Final New Source Performance Standards and Emissions Guidelines for the Crude Oil and Natural Gas Sector Climate Review, Table 1-6

rows.explainer: Equivalent annualized value at 2% over 2024-2038, million 2019 dollars: $1.5 billion a year, net of the recovered gas the operators sell ($0.98 billion of a gross $2.4 billion). Range: $1 billion (ex-post costs below ex-ante, as is common) to the gross $2.4 billion (gas worth less).

rows.label: EPA power-plant carbon standards (2024): compliance cost a year, 2024-2047 (2019 dollars)

source.title: US EPA (2024), Carbon pollution standards: fact sheet on the standards and regulatory impact analysis (RIA Table ES-2)
source.quote: $270 billion in climate benefits; $120 billion in health benefits; and $19 billion in compliance costs

rows.explainer: Present value $19 billion at 2% over 2024-2047, $0.98 billion a year annualized (2019 dollars): the modelled change in the power system's capital, operating, fuel and CO₂ storage costs, so fuel changes are already netted, and tax credits (transfers) left out. Range: $0.65 billion (EPA's 7% figure, a proxy for costs coming in lower) to $1.5 billion (costlier capture and storage).

rows.label: EPA light- and medium-duty vehicle standards (2024): buyers' net cost a year, 2027-2055 (2022 dollars; negative is a saving)

source.title: US EPA (2024), Multi-Pollutant Emissions Standards for Model Years 2027 and Later Light-Duty and Medium-Duty Vehicles, final rule, 89 FR 27842, Table 8
source.quote: The annualized value of vehicle technology costs is estimated at $40 billion.

rows.explainer: Annualized at 2%, 2022 dollars: vehicle technology $40 billion, chargers $9 billion and insurance $1.5 billion a year, less pre-tax fuel savings of $46 billion and maintenance and repair savings of $15.8 billion, which go to the same buyers: a net saving of $11.3 billion a year. The model counts only the tonnes and the air, so the buyers' net money is counted here. Range: a saving of $25 billion (cheaper batteries) to a cost of $5 billion (fuel savings half EPA's).

rows.label: California's Advanced Clean Cars II: owners' net cost a year, 2026-2040 (2020 dollars; negative is a saving)

source.title: California Air Resources Board (2022), Advanced Clean Cars II, Final Statement of Reasons, Appendix F: updated costs and benefits
source.quote: the total net cost from 2026 to 2040 decreased from -$81.8 billion to -92.9 billion (2020 dollars)

rows.explainer: CARB counts owners' costs of $210.3 billion (vehicles, electricity, hydrogen, insurance, registration, sales tax) against savings of $303.2 billion (gasoline at retail, maintenance, vehicle-to-grid) over 2026-2040, undiscounted: a net saving of $92.9 billion, $6.2 billion a year (the low end). Taxes are transfers, not costs: taking out registration and sales tax ($15.2 billion) and the fuel taxes in the gasoline price (about a quarter, $54 billion) leaves a saving of about $23 billion, $1.6 billion a year. Our judgment on the taxes; range to a cost of $1 billion a year (savings overstated).

rows.label: California's cap-and-invest extension: businesses' and households' net cost a year, 2027-2046, allowance transfers out (2024 dollars)

source.title: California Air Resources Board (2026), Proposed amendments to the Cap-and-Invest Program, Initial Statement of Reasons, chapter VIII (economic impacts)
source.quote: Total Direct Costs (Compliance + Abatement Costs) ($ billion) $123.8

rows.explainer: CARB's 2027-2046 direct costs less allowance transfers are $110.8 billion, against cost savings of $57.8 billion (2024 dollars): a net $53 billion, $2.65 billion a year. Range $1.5 billion (savings larger) to $4.5 billion (abatement costlier, as the 2024 SRIA's gross $98.5 billion of abatement for the earlier proposal suggests).

rows.label: EU Methane Regulation: exporters' abatement cost per tonne of CO₂e cut by the import measures (2018 dollars)

source.title: European Commission (2021), Impact assessment accompanying the proposal for a regulation on methane emissions reduction in the energy sector, SWD(2021) 459, policy area 3 and Annex 5, Table A.5.6
source.quote: The total costs of measures to achieve socially and environmentally cost effective methane emission reductions in those key exporting countries amounts to 2,607 million USD (or 2,216 million Euros).

rows.explainer: The impact assessment didn't cost the import obligations, which were added in negotiation; as a proxy it costed the cost-effective cuts in the eight main exporters to the EU by 2030: $2,607 million (2018 dollars, from the IEA's cost curves, net of the gas saved and sold) for 25.5 million tonnes of methane, about 714 million tonnes of CO₂e at its own factor of 28: $3.65 a tonne. Range $1 (more of the cut pays for itself) to $10 (the import standard reaches costlier sources than the cheapest cuts).

rows.label: EPA fine-particle standard (2024, 9 µg/m³): control costs a year in 2032 (2017 dollars)

source.title: US EPA (2024), Regulatory Impact Analysis for the Final Reconsideration of the National Ambient Air Quality Standards for Particulate Matter, Table ES-10

rows.explainer: Control costs of $590 million in 2032 for the 9/35 standard (2017 dollars, annualized at 7%); $470 million a year equivalent over 2032-2051 at 3% (the low end). The controls EPA modelled don't reach the standard in some counties, so the costs are incomplete: high end the $1.5 billion of the tighter 8 µg/m³ option.

rows.label: EPA PFAS drinking-water standards (2024): costs a year (2022 dollars)

source.title: US EPA (2024), PFAS National Primary Drinking Water Regulation, final rule, 89 FR 32532
source.quote: the quantifiable annual benefits of the final rule will be $1,549.40 million per year and the quantifiable costs of the rule will be $1,548.64 million per year

rows.explainer: Annualized at 2%, in 2022 dollars (the rule's price year), almost all water systems' treatment, disposal and monitoring ($1,543 million), passed to ratepayers; EPA's quantified benefits are the same size. Range: $1.2 billion (treatment cheaper than projected) to $3 billion (the water utilities' own estimates are higher).

rows.label: EPA Lead and Copper Rule Improvements (2024): costs a year (2022 dollars)

source.title: US EPA (2024), National Primary Drinking Water Regulations for Lead and Copper: Improvements (LCRI), final rule, 89 FR 86418
source.quote: quantifiable annual costs of the rule will be $1.47 to $1.95 billion in 2022 dollars

rows.explainer: Annualized at 2% over 35 years, 2022 dollars, most of it replacing lead service lines ($1.17 to $1.64 billion), paid by water systems and passed to ratepayers. EPA's range; the middle as the best guess.

rows.label: UK Tobacco and Vapes Act, smokefree generation: costs a year, 2027-2056 (2019 pounds)

source.title: Department of Health and Social Care (2024), Tobacco and Vapes Bill: impact assessment
source.quote: Net Benefit (Present Value (PV)) (£m) Low: Optional High: Optional Best Estimate: 18,584.7

rows.explainer: The impact assessment puts the smokefree generation's costs at £1,913.5 million in present value (2019 prices, base year 2020, 2027-2056 at 3.5%; benefits £20,498.2 million), mostly retailers' and wholesalers' lost profits; lost duty (£26.1 billion) is a transfer and left out. As a yearly equivalent: £1,913.5 million carried to 2027 (× 1.035^7) over a 30-year annuity at 3.5% (18.39), £132.4 million a year. Range £80 million (shoppers spend the money on other goods sold by the same shops) to £250 million (with the manufacturers' lost profits the assessment leaves out, £587 million for England, as their owners abroad still lose).

rows.label: California Proposition 12 regulations (eggs, pork, veal): yearly cost net of retailers' extra profit (2020 dollars)

source.title: California Department of Food and Agriculture (2021), Animal Confinement: Notice of Proposed Action, summary of the Standardized Regulatory Impact Assessment (SRIA)
source.quote: In the 2022 calendar year, proposed regulations will increase consumer expenditures in California of $1,195 million.
source.note: The SRIA's gross figure is the extra that Californians spend on covered shell and liquid eggs, pork and veal in 2022. The Department of Finance's comments on the SRIA (August 2020, dof.ca.gov CDFA_Prop_12_SRIA_Finance_Comments_August_2020.pdf, no longer online; read from search summaries, retrieved 2026-11-15) put about $950 million of it in shell-egg retailers' extra profit and about $18 million in liquid-egg retailers', with pork and veal retailers' profits falling, and note that producers' compliance costs are not quantified. Retailers' profit is a transfer from shoppers to retailers' owners, so it is left out, while pork retailers' lost profit (about $63 million) is a real cost: 1,195 - 950 - 18 + 63, about $290 million, rounded to $300 million a year. The notice itself gives California's egg producers' extra costs as $72 million (p. 14). Written in 2020, so taken as 2020 dollars.

rows.explainer: The regulator's analysis of Proposition 12's rules: Californians spend about $1.2 billion a year more on covered eggs, pork and veal, of which about $0.9 billion is retailers' extra margin on shell eggs, a transfer. Best guess $300 million a year net. Range: $150 million (our judgment: the projection was for the first year, before supply adjusted) to the gross $1,195 million (if the margin is a shortage cost rather than a transfer).

rows.label: UK ban on cages for laying hens (consultation 2026): direct cost to business a year (pounds)
rows.explainer: Our judgment, anchored on Defra's consultation-stage de minimis assessment of the laying hen cage reform (12 January 2026, consult.defra.gov.uk, laying-hen-cage-reform supporting documents; the page no longer loads, retrieved 2026-11-15): a de minimis assessment is the UK's form for measures whose equivalent annual net direct cost to business is under £5 million, which bounds the cost, and most colony cages would be near the end of their life by the proposed 2032 deadline. Best guess £3 million a year, range £1-5 million.
